from rich.highlighter import ReprHighlighter
from rich.text import Text

highlighter = ReprHighlighter()
# A URL with '@' in it (common in basic auth)
url = "https://user:pass@example.com"
text = Text(url)
highlighted = highlighter.highlight(text)

# If highlighting works, the entire URL should be tagged with 'url' style.
# ReprHighlighter applies styles to the Text object.
# Since we can't easily check the internal style of a Text object without iterating,
# we can check the spans.

# We expect the entire string to be marked as 'url'.
# In a failing case, the '@' likely breaks the regex, and it might be split.

expected_style = "url"
assert highlighted.spans[0].style == expected_style, f"Expected style {expected_style}, got {highlighted.spans[0].style}"
assert highlighted.spans[0].start == 0
assert highlighted.spans[0].end == len(url)
assert len(highlighted.spans) == 1, f"Expected 1 span, got {len(highlighted.spans)}: {highlighted.spans}"
EOF

steps.message:
FILES: rich/highlighter.py:101
CAUSE: The URL regex pattern in `ReprHighlighter` does not include the `@` character, which causes it to stop matching when a URL contains user authentication (e.g., `https://user:pass@example.com`).
FIX: Add `@` to the character set in the `url` regex pattern in `ReprHighlighter.highlights`.
REPRO: 
```python
from rich.highlighter import ReprHighlighter
from rich.text import Text

highlighter = ReprHighlighter()
url = "https://user:pass@example.com/path"
text = Text(url)
highlighter.highlight(text)
# CURRENTLY: text.spans is [Span(0, 17, 'repr.url')], which stops at '@'
# EXPECTED: text.spans is [Span(0, 32, 'repr.url')]
assert len(text.spans) == 1 and text.spans[0].end == len(url)
```
TESTS: tests/test_highlighter.py
